notes: IMPORTANT: a finding's `line` is the SINK CALL site, not the method declaration. The manifest lines below are the measured sink lines.

anchor_fn names the ENCLOSING METHOD that should OWN the finding. For the deep cross-file chains the owner is the ORCHESTRATOR method, because the engine must attribute the finding to the caller that carries the taint. If instead the finding is attributed to the sink method with the sink's own parameter as the taint source, the chain has NOT been followed and the case scores FN.

On this build every deep-chain case scores FN while every intra-procedural control scores PASS. That difference is the measurement. TN cases pass VACUOUSLY for the deep chains, because no finding is produced at all.

Measured control result: `dfa-taint-sql-injection` fires at SqlSink.java lines 24 (executeQuery), 31 (executeUpdate), and 65 (inTryCatch). `dfa-taint-command-injection` fires at NonSqlSink 48 (ProcessBuilder) and 54 (Runtime.exec). `dfa-taint-path-traversal` fires at NonSqlSink 29, 37, 38.
